body: Pokémon Colosseum is Genius Sonority's GameCube role-playing adventure set in the desert region of Orre. Wes, a former member of Team Snagem, travels with Rui to rescue Shadow Pokémon whose hearts have been closed by the organisation Cipher. These creatures are captured from opposing trainers rather than found through ordinary wild encounters. The premise gives the familiar act of throwing a Poké Ball another purpose. Acquiring a new companion begins with recognising that something has been done to it, then taking responsibility for helping it recover.

Most encounters use Double Battles, putting two Pokémon on each side of the field. The player has to consider how the pair's moves and vulnerabilities work together, while keeping the targeted Shadow Pokémon alive long enough to capture it. Rui identifies the creatures that need rescuing. Purification then makes their recovery part of the longer journey rather than the end of a single fight. The party develops through both kinds of work: winning the next encounter and caring for the unusual new member brought out of it.

Towns, colosseums and hostile bases connect the battles into an adventure with its own protagonist and supporting cast. Tsukasa Tawada's music gives Orre a distinctive sound alongside the much larger presentation of familiar Pokémon. Game Boy Advance connectivity allows trading and further battles with the handheld games. Released in Japan in 2003, Colosseum gave the home console more than another arena for a collection built elsewhere. Its rescue story established a separate place in which a new team could be assembled and developed through the player's own journey.
